title: Packet Trail Inspector — request drilldown & correlation UX prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket covers a high-fidelity prototype and interaction spec for the new "Packet Trail Inspector" — a unified request drilldown surface in Redwood Console that helps engineers inspect spans, timeline lanes, correlation IDs, cross-service hops, and inline cost attribution. The goal is to enable fast root-cause workflows for latency, cost spikes, and functional errors without leaving the Console. The design combines a horizontally scrollable timeline, stacked span lanes, a correlation sidecar, and an overlay for rollout/flag metadata to show whether a request hit a new model or rollout variant.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows timeline with virtualized span lanes for traces up to 30k spans
Correlation ID sidecar surfaces all sibling requests across services and regions
Inline cost attribution bubble shows token-level cost estimate for the request and a breakdown by model variant
Interaction spec includes hover-to-scrub, range-select to snapshot, and shareable permalink generation
Design includes fallback for sampled traces and an indicator for sampling rate and sampling reason
Accessibility: keyboard navigation through spans, ARIA labels for timeline lanes, and color-blind safe palette
decisions: Reuse existing Timeline component but extend it to support multi-lane virtualization and span grouping
Correlation sidecar implemented as detachable panel (can be detached into a floating inspector) to support multi-monitor workflows
Cost attribution will be estimated client-side using the runtime cost model, with server-side verification in a follow-up backend ticket
Rollout overlay will pull from the rollout API; if rollout metadata is missing, show a graceful message and default to 'unknown variant' state
We will not attempt to render full stack traces for spans that exceed tokenized view threshold; instead provide a compressed summary and link to raw logs
